card.title: Are all infinities the same size?

body.question: There are infinitely many whole numbers and infinitely many real numbers. Is one infinity bigger than the other?
options: Yes, the real numbers are a bigger infinity
Yes, the whole numbers are bigger
body.reveal: Cantor's diagonal argument shows there are infinite sets that cannot be matched one-to-one with the natural numbers. Such sets are called uncountable. Meanwhile the even numbers can be matched with all natural numbers by doubling, so an infinite set can have the same size as a part of itself.

probes.question: True or false: the even numbers can be matched one-to-one with the natural numbers.
What is a set called if it cannot be put into one-to-one correspondence with the natural numbers?

claims.claim: Cantor's diagonal argument shows infinite sets that cannot be matched one-to-one with the natural numbers; called uncountable
claims.quote: there are infinite sets which cannot be put into one-to-one correspondence with the infinite set of natural numbers
claims.note: Page: 'Such sets are now called uncountable sets'.

claims.claim: The real numbers are the bigger (uncountable) infinity
claims.quote: Georg Cantor published this proof in 1891, but it was not his first proof of the uncountability of the real numbers

claims.claim: The even numbers match the natural numbers by doubling; an infinite set can equal a part of itself in size
claims.quote: An infinite set may have the same cardinality as a proper subset of itself, as the depicted bijection f ( x )=2 x from the natural to the even numbers demonstrates.
